Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — evidence & escrow requirements

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Greenwood is evaluating Redwood for an on-prem deployment across three data centers. Our legal team needs clearer language on two points before we can proceed to procurement:

1) License scope — we need confirmation that the license for on-prem includes runtime redistribution to our internal hosting teams and limited sublicensing to our cloud ops partner (no broader transfer).
2) Audit / escrow alternatives — instead of full source escrow, Greenwood requires either (a) source escrow or (b) a documented attestation plus a third-party code escrow of runtime artifacts. We also need a documented incident recovery procedure (keys, custody) and an evidence package for encryption and key custody.

Attached: SourceEscrow_Proposal.pdf with Greenwood’s standard language. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept attestation plus runtime artifact escrow (as opposed to source escrow), and provide a draft addendum?

Best,
Sara Lawson
Senior Counsel, Greenwood Health

Aditya —

Thanks. Quick thoughts after reviewing Greenwood’s PDF:

- License scope: we can accept explicit language that permits internal redistribution to Greenwood-controlled infrastructure and one named cloud-ops partner, provided the addendum includes a non-transfer clause and limits on sublicensing (timebound and purpose-limited). I’ll draft redline that lists the partner by name when they provide it; prefer to avoid open-ended sublicensing.

- Escrow: source escrow is high risk for us (IP exposure). Acceptable compromise: (1) runtime artifact escrow (binaries, container images, checksums) deposited with an independent escrow agent, coupled with (2) quarterly attestation from Redwood’s CTO about build reproducibility and a documented emergency access process (KMS/HSM key custody chain-of-custody and escrow release triggers).

- Evidence package: agree to provide cryptographic proofs (code signing keys, build logs) and SOC2/AICPA evidence where available, plus a runbook for incident recovery. We should tie disclosure triggers to narrow conditions (bankruptcy, prolonged failure to support for X months, insolvency, or material breach) — not routine audits.

I’ll prepare two things: a redlined MSA clause for license + sublicensing limits, and an addendum for the Private Deployment that defines escrow alternative (runtime artifacts + attestation), release triggers, third-party escrow agent role, and a list of evidence items we can commit to.

Two asks for sales:
1) Have Greenwood name their cloud-ops partner (for license language).
2) Decide commercial leverage: do we offer this as standard for Dedicated or only at enterprise addendum / fee?

Will send redlines by EOD tomorrow.

- Laura
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sara —

Thanks for the detail. We reviewed Greenwood’s proposal and can offer an alternative path that preserves Greenwood’s risk profile without full source escrow:

1) License: Redwood will grant an on-prem runtime license that permits redistribution to Greenwood-controlled infrastructure and one named cloud-ops partner (specified in the addendum). Sublicensing must be purpose-limited (operations only) and non-transferable without Redwood’s written consent.

2) Escrow alternative: instead of source escrow, Redwood proposes:
   - Deposit of runtime artifacts (container images, signed binaries, checksums) with an independent escrow agent;
   - Quarterly CTO attestation confirming build reproducibility and availability of build logs;
   - A documented emergency release process (release triggers: insolvency, failure to support for 6 consecutive months, or court order).

3) Evidence package: provide code-signing certificates, build logs, SOC2 report excerpts (redacted), and a custody matrix for keys. Routine audits will be limited to an annual compliance attestation; direct access to IP or source will not be granted without the narrow release triggers noted.

Attached is a draft Private_Deployment_Addendum_draft.docx that implements the above. Laura is copying in a redline for the MSA license language.

If Greenwood can accept the escrow-alternative language, we can proceed to finalize the Order Form and commercial terms. Otherwise, Laura will outline what would be required to accept source escrow (pricing, timelines, and escrow agent controls).

Would Greenwood be open to naming their cloud-ops partner so we can include it in the addendum?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Private_Deployment_Addendum_draft.docx (docx)
From: Tom Bradley <tom.bradley@greenwoodhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, sara.lawson@greenwoodhealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence & escrow requirements

Aditya / Laura,

Thanks for the detailed alternative. Greenwood can provisionally accept runtime artifact escrow + quarterly attestation, but two items to confirm before legal will finalize:

1) Escrow agent — Greenwood requires the escrow agent to be a neutral third party with specific certification (e.g., Iron Mountain or EscrowTech). Can Redwood provide a list of acceptable agents or confirm willingness to use a Greenwood-preferred agent?
2) Release triggers — Greenwood requests that "support failure" be defined more narrowly (e.g., failure to remediate a Severity 1 production outage within 30 days after documented remediation plan, not a blanket 6-month clause).

If Redwood can accept named agents or an impartial selection process and tighten the remediation trigger, I think legal will sign off. Also, we prefer that attestation reports be retained for three years.

Tom Bradley
Director, Cloud Operations, Greenwood Health
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

All —

Updated position after Tom’s note: accept named escrow agents (we can agree to Iron Mountain or EscrowTech; I will add a fallback of mutual selection if Greenwood insists on a different vendor).

Re: release triggers — we will narrow the support-failure trigger to: failure to remediate a Severity 1 production outage within 30 days following agreement on a remediation plan (with periodic status updates). That aligns with our incident processes and avoids an open-ended clause.

Retention: we will retain attestation artifacts for three years, redacted where necessary.

Commercial ask: if Greenwood requires source-code escrow rather than the runtime-alternative, we will need to price the additional operational and compliance overhead (estimated uplift 15–25% of the annual contract) and agree SLA terms for escrow custody. Prefer to avoid that.

Next steps (action items):
- Laura to deliver redlined MSA clause + addendum with named agent options (EOD tomorrow).
- Aditya to confirm sales position on whether we charge extra for the runtime-escrow alternative (recommendation: include as part of enterprise private deployment at no additional fee for now; revisit after closing).
- Marissa/Karthik to confirm approval for using Iron Mountain / EscrowTech or mutual selection.

If we’re all aligned, I’ll send the redlines to Sara/Tom and ask for Greenwood’s partner name.

- Laura
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
